content:
The late Princess Diana's brother, Charles Spencer, has shared his thoughts on the ongoing rift between Princes William and Harry.

Speaking in an exclusive interview with the BBC, Spencer said: "I think there's a perception in the media that I am on Harry's side. In fact, I am on the side of my late sister's two sons – I support them both." The interview aired on Sunday to coincide with the publication of his new book about Diana, *Swan Song: My Sister, Diana*.

The historian added: "If either of them needs me, I will be there for them equally." He continued: "I never take sides with either camp. I just hope to be a pleasant presence."

Speaking about the broken relationship between Harry and William, Spencer noted that things having "reached this point" was the result of "a lot of reasons on both sides."

He shared: "I hope one day things will be resolved, but I don't know the full picture. I certainly don't know the details, so if I got too involved, I would feel presumptuous. A mother would of course want her two sons to be happy and loving towards each other."

In an interview with *People* magazine, Spencer also touched on another topic of interest to royal watchers: when he told the two princes about the new book.

Spencer said: "I told them both at the same time, and all I can say is one of them… I told all four of them at the same time (William, Harry, and Spencer's two sisters, Sarah and Jane)." He added: "Let's just say Harry was absolutely fine with it."

The historian shared: "He said, 'I just hope there's nothing in there that's going to embarrass me.' I said, 'There won't be.' I think they had been worrying about the direction of the book, really." He added that the book "basically ends when Diana died in 1997."

He added: "But I can put both their minds at rest – they are in the book, of course, but mainly as examples of two little boys who had the most extraordinary mother. I haven't intruded on their privacy in any way at all."

Spencer's new book was published on Tuesday, ahead of the 30th anniversary of Diana's death (31 August 1997).
